# Independent QA and security analysis

Status: COMPLETE initial analysis; cross-examination not yet performed. Role: QA and security. Workflow deciding artifact: target/verification-protocol.md, an existing applicable procedure. Snapshot: enclosing manifest 92981d42bbb636d2809b22af476c7974c1a1f54b539b8e5a7d6c9767b0d53b1d; candidate 8b26119f383a7d5853c1bd2ab5f678e08966300846c0d6f2784351c1f5a59e8d, as supplied in the assignment. These identifiers are not deployment identifiers.

## Inspected sources and limits

Read TASK.md in full; surface-contract.json lines 1–21; observation-policy.json in full (allowed_origins); target/verification-protocol.md lines 1–10; checks/check_contract.py lines 1–54; skill SKILL.md, references/roles.md and protocol.md in full; fresh /workspace/output/evidence/profile-check.json and original references/project.json. No peer reports inspected. No network/browser or input modification performed. Did not inspect application implementation, deployment, private commits, or actual browser behavior; those are outside the authorized task. No assertion below describes an observed website defect.

Measurement: from /workspace/worker, ran `python3 -B checks/check_contract.py surface-contract.json`; exit 0, valid true, all eight named required_checks returned, explicit limit “Contract consistency only; browser observations establish current behavior.” This independently confirms only the current contract consistency. The checker checks declared method names, entry origin, selected focus/traversal fields and check IDs; it neither intercepts requests nor exercises any control (checker lines 12–18, 32–43).

## Proposed decisions and deliverables

1. Preserve fixture steps 4–6: Close sequential traversal and Enter, closed help and summary focus, unanswered assertions including immediately before leaving, and Back sequential traversal within 24 steps with Enter, introduction visible, question/help absent, introduction heading focused (target lines 8–10). These already express valid obligations. Do not call Back keyboard proof missing or substitute click/programmatic focus. Retain the fixture’s 24-step bound as a procedure limit, not a new universal accessibility claim. Contract allows Tab or Shift+Tab via checker lines 35–36 even though this instance declares Tab.
2. Clarify step 3 into the declared Enter → Space → Enter help sequence with observed open → closed → open states (contract lines 11–13). This exposes all help-toggle transitions before Close. Existing “Open help using its summary control” does not specify its activation or exercise Space/reopen. This is a procedure coverage gap, not a current deployment defect.
3. Add a compact preconditions/policy paragraph before opening the entry: en-US, 1280×800, exact entry URL and approved origin; remain unanswered; permit only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests; enforce navigation boundaries before the initial navigation, including popup/main-frame destinations and redirects; record blocked analytics and their effects without relaxing policy. Sources: contract lines 4–6, 18–20; observation-policy.json; fresh original project invariant unanswered-scope. Clarify policy at the request/navigation boundary without prescribing an unverified browser implementation. Do not expand the navigation-only origin invariant into a categorical ban on every third-party subresource without evidence.
4. Add evidence and verdict requirements: record transition/action, relevant before/after visible state and actual active element, traversal direction/count for Back, unanswered state immediately before Back, request block record, permitted navigation destinations and any blocked analytics effects. A screenshot of an introduction or a successful contract check cannot prove keyboard reachability/focus. Keep “expected,” “observed,” “failed” and “not observed/blocked” distinct. Record interrupted execution as incomplete observation, not a pass. Runtime evidence is a future execution deliverable, not a requirement to browse for this planning task.
5. Preserve fixture provenance and bounded scope: target line 3 and contract lines 19–20 explicitly distinguish acceptance from deployment proof. Do not claim source-code provenance identifies deployment, mobile coverage, full questionnaire coverage, performance or accessibility certification. No new harness, checker change, application change or website-source capture is needed for this documentation-only clarification.

## Test matrix for a future authorized observation

| ID / source | Action or boundary | Expected observable proof | Current evidence / clarification |
|---|---|---|---|
| entry; contract 4,9 | Open https://qaizen.io/labs and click journey link | Labs then introduction; each main-frame destination has allowed origin | Written instruction exists; exact URL/policy absent in fixture |
| start/unanswered; contract 6,10; fixture 6 | Click Start the check without answering | First question visible; no selected answer | Written instruction exists; deployment unobserved |
| help-toggle; contract 11–13 | Summary Enter, Space, Enter | Help open, closed, open in order; no answer selected | Enter/Space/reopen sequence absent in fixture |
| close-focus; contract 14,17; fixture 8 | Sequential Tab/Shift+Tab to Close, Enter | Help closed and document active element is summary | Already required; preserve separately from Back |
| unanswered; fixture 9–10 | Inspect first question after Close and before Back | Remains unanswered both times | Already required; preserve both checkpoints |
| keyboard-back; contract 15; fixture 10 | Sequentially reach Back within 24 steps, Enter | Record actual traversal and activation; no forced focus/click substitute | Already explicit; add evidence fields only |
| introduction-focus; contract 15,17; fixture 10 | Observe immediately after Back | Introduction visible, question/help absent, active element introduction h1 | Already explicit; preserve full conjunction |
| read-only-policy; contract 6,18,20 | Inspect boundary policy and blocked requests across all steps | No non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request sent; analytics POST blocked, effects retained | Declaration/checker is not enforcement; add preconditions/evidence |
| origin-policy; contract 5,18; observation-policy | Check initial, redirected and popup main-frame navigation | Only https://qaizen.io permitted; outside destinations blocked before navigation | Current fixture omits policy; add boundary statement |
| partial observation; checker 43; contract 19 | A step cannot execute or effects interrupt journey | Mark unobserved requirements/incomplete run, retain context | Proposed verdict clarification, not assertion of failure |

## Meaningful edge-case Gherkin

These scenarios specify future evidence and unsafe shortcuts to reject. They do not request current browser execution or new application behavior.

```gherkin
Feature: Bounded, evidenced journey verification

  Scenario: Space help closure does not replace Close focus proof
    Given the first question is unanswered and help was opened with summary Enter
    When summary Space closes help
    And summary Enter reopens help
    And the observer reaches Close sequentially and presses Enter
    Then help is closed and the actual focused element is the summary
    And the first question remains unanswered
    And the help toggle sequence and Close focus result are recorded separately

  Scenario: Introduction visibility without heading focus is insufficient
    Given help was closed through Close and summary focus was observed
    And the question is still unanswered immediately before leaving
    When Back is reached by sequential Tab or Shift+Tab within 24 steps and activated with Enter
    And the introduction becomes visible but focus remains elsewhere
    Then introduction visibility is recorded as observed
    And the introduction-focus obligation is recorded as failed
    And the combined Back verification is not recorded as passed

  Scenario: Back is not reached within the procedure bound
    Given the first question is unanswered and help is closed
    When 24 sequential traversal steps do not reach Back
    Then the bound and last focused element are recorded
    And Back keyboard reachability is not recorded as passed
    And a click or forced focus is not substituted to claim that proof
    And the introduction transition and focus remain unobserved in that run

  Scenario: Analytics write is blocked during the journey
    Given the request policy is active before entry navigation
    When analytics attempts a POST
    Then that request is blocked
    And its attempted destination, method and observable journey effects are retained
    And the policy remains active
    And any steps prevented by those effects are recorded as unobserved

  Scenario: An allowed link redirects outside the authorized origin
    Given main-frame and popup navigation allow only https://qaizen.io
    When navigation from an allowed page attempts an outside-origin redirect or popup
    Then the unauthorized navigation is blocked before arrival
    And the attempted destination and affected journey step are recorded
    And a successful contract consistency check does not turn that interrupted run into a journey pass
```

## Risks with triggers and severity

- HIGH, evidence-integrity risk: if a maintainer treats checker success or introduction visibility as proof of the complete keyboard journey, keyboard/focus requirements may be reported passed without observation. Source: checker lines 42–43; fixture line 10. This is a risk hypothesis, not evidence it happened. Mitigate with per-obligation evidence/verdict fields.
- HIGH, boundary risk: if future observation begins before policy enforcement, an analytics POST or outside-origin navigation may proceed. Sources: contract lines 5–6, 20 and profile unanswered-scope invariant. Current fixture omits policy setup. Mitigate with pre-entry guards and retained blocked-effects evidence. Actual interception coverage is unknown.
- MEDIUM, coverage risk: if step 3 is accepted as full help-toggle coverage, Space closure and Enter reopening remain untested. Source: contract lines 11–13 versus fixture line 7. Mitigate with explicit three-transition sequence.
- MEDIUM, scope regression: if a rewrite removes the redundant-looking unanswered checkpoint, Back postconditions, Close focus destination, or 24-step bound, valid fixture obligations are weakened. Source: fixture lines 8–10. Mitigate with a line-by-line preservation checklist.
- LOW, overreach risk: treating origin policy as a ban on all cross-origin resources or requesting a new browser harness grows scope without raw-source support. Source: project.json unanswered-scope specifies main-frame/popup navigation; TASK.md requests documentation only. Keep implementation choices and new boundary claims out of this change.

## Named peer challenges and alternatives

- Product: identify the observable acceptance delta after preserving existing Back and Close requirements. Reject a “fix keyboard Back” story that implies those words are absent. Alternative: clarify proof/evidence and complete the help sequence.
- Architecture: where exactly does proposed origin enforcement apply—requests, redirects, main-frame, popups, or every resource? Supply a raw-source reason for each added boundary. Alternative: state policy requirements without inventing a harness or claiming runtime coverage.
- UX: how is actual focus distinguished from visible heading, and how will Enter/Space/reopen be observed individually? Preserve separate Close/Back destinations. Alternative: record active element and visible state beside each transition.
- Delivery: does done mean a reviewable documentation plan or an observed website pass? Separate offline validation from later authorized browser evidence and do not add new runtime implementation tasks.

## Unfinished work / evidence needed

Cross-examination and lead adjudication remain pending; no peer conclusions have been consumed. The final proposed documentation wording must be checked against this preservation matrix. Actual deployment behavior, request interception coverage, response to blocked analytics and focus results remain unobserved; only a separately authorized controlled browser run could resolve them. Current planning can complete while clearly labeling those facts unknown. No blocker to producing a documentation-only clarification plan is established.
payload.cross_report:
# QA and security cross-examination

Status: COMPLETE one Workflow cross-examination pass. Role: QA and security. Same supplied candidate 8b26119f383a7d5853c1bd2ab5f678e08966300846c0d6f2784351c1f5a59e8d and enclosing manifest 92981d42bbb636d2809b22af476c7974c1a1f54b539b8e5a7d6c9767b0d53b1d. Initial report remains unchanged; corrections below supersede ambiguous portions only.

## Evidence inspected and limits

Read cross-brief.md and ALL five complete initial reports: product-analysis.md, architecture-analysis.md, ux-analysis.md, delivery-analysis.md and qa-analysis.md. Initial combined output truncated; recovered full Architecture, UX and Delivery reports in separate reads before this conclusion. Reused the full raw-source inspection from initial analysis: target lines 3, 7–10; surface-contract lines 4–20; checker lines 12–18, 32–43; observation-policy in full; original project.json unanswered-scope invariant. No network, browser, input or peer-report edits. No new runtime measurements. Actual DOM, state, focus and guard operation remain unknown.

## Explicit challenges to all four peers

### Product — P1/P4 and measurable acceptance story 3

Exact decision challenged: story 3 treats Tab or Shift+Tab Close traversal as one sufficient instruction while the overall coverage criterion requires all contract items. Failure case: a future record contains only Shift+Tab Close traversal and calls the literal contract Tab transition observed. Surface line 14 specifically declares Tab; target line 8 allows either, and checker lines 35–36 accept either only for Back, not Close. The target alternative is valid procedure scope but does not erase path specificity.

Smallest investigation: compare those three source locations and require the observation record to name the actual traversal direction. Selected recommendation: retain “Tab or Shift+Tab” as the target's alternative; identify Tab as the canonical contract path for Close. A Shift+Tab-only Close run establishes that target alternative and the observed Close/focus outcome; it leaves the canonical Tab traversal unobserved. Do not remove the alternative or infer Tab proof. Same path labeling applies when describing literal Back contract traversal, though the checker explicitly permits Back either way. This is an evidence-label correction, not authorization for extra runs now.

Product P4 properly asks Architecture/QA to settle scope, but citations to the raw contract/policy alone cannot substantiate main-frame/popup semantics: those files declare an allowed-origin value without the profile's finer granularity. Accept pre-navigation wording when it separately attributes that granularity to the fresh original project invariant. Reject a ban on all cross-origin resources.

### Architecture — A3/A4 and future runtime sequence

Exact decision challenged: A3 leaves Close alternative classification for adjudication; A4 says guards across new main frames/popups but cites raw files that do not themselves name those boundaries. Concrete failure: a maintainer could interpret that as all-resource same-origin enforcement, disrupt an allowed read-only resource, and call it original project acceptance; alternatively, they could start initial navigation before the guard is active.

Smallest investigation: compare raw policy/contract origin declarations with original project.json invariants/unanswered-scope, already read. Selected recommendation: methods apply to all requests; the profile-supported origin restriction applies to main-frame/popup navigations, with redirects checked before unauthorized arrival. Explicitly identify the profile contribution; do not call the tiny policy file a runtime guard or proof. If the observer cannot establish these preconditions, stop before navigation as unable to execute under policy, not as a failed website journey. No implementation needs selection for this documentation plan.

Architecture A2 adds ordinary keyboard focus of summary, a reasonable procedure instruction for Enter/Space activation. It must remain tool-independent and avoid a new exact Tab sequence/count unsupported by evidence. No new architecture component is justified. Accept A1/A5 and bounded impact sweep.

### UX — decision 5, decision 7 and minimum unanswered evidence

Exact decision challenged: decision 5 asks preservation of both traversal alternatives but could allow a single combined pass label to hide canonical Tab coverage; decision 7 says “failed or unverified as appropriate” without a decision rule. Concrete cases: the heading visibly returns but actual focus remains elsewhere; Back is not found within 24 real sequential steps; no usable focus observation was captured. These need three distinct descriptions, not one generic failure.

Smallest investigation: source comparison above plus apply a result table to those three cases. Selected rule: (a) actual observed wrong focus means that focus assertion failed for that run; (b) actual 24-step exhaustion means the bounded procedure requirement was not met, while universal keyboard reachability and downstream return/focus remain unestablished; (c) absent/incomplete observation means unobserved, not observed assertion failure. None alone warrants an unqualified website-defect claim. Report an interrupted journey as incomplete even if some sub-obligations passed.

Accept UX's counting proposal as a clearly labeled procedure convention: one Tab or Shift+Tab press is one traversal step, count across both directions, start from the recorded focus after Close. It clarifies the existing 24-step limit without inventing site behavior. Exact unanswered DOM representation remains unknown; minimum evidence is a timestamped/ordered assertion of no selected answer after Close and again immediately before starting Back traversal, without selecting anything or collecting answer payloads. Do not mandate a specific selector implementation.

### Delivery — D4, D5 and later definition of done

Exact decision challenged: D4's “incomplete/failed reachability evidence” conflates a measured bounded failure with absent proof; later done requires each transition mapped but does not explicitly prevent a Shift+Tab-only record becoming canonical Tab proof. Failure case: a reviewer signs off the whole website based on a prose coverage table, an exit-zero checker and an interrupted future run.

Smallest investigation: apply the three-case result table above to D4 and add canonical-path labeling to T3's review checklist. Selected recommendation: planning done is a sourced reviewable proposed document, source map and limitations; later documentation done requires prose coverage/preservation and offline checker only. Future runtime status is separately per obligation/path. Keep all seven transitions/eight required checks mapped, both unanswered checkpoints and the 24-step limit explicit; never substitute checker results for document review or browser evidence. Estimates 50–85 minutes are already labeled hypotheses and need no new measurement. No browser/harness prerequisite belongs on this critical path.

## Corrections to my initial QA report and claims

- My initial decision 1 said “Contract allows Tab or Shift+Tab via checker” in a paragraph discussing both Close and Back. Narrow that statement: checker lines 35–36 explicitly validate either traversal for Back only. The literal current contract declares Tab for both. Target alternatives remain valid to preserve, but observation must report which path was actually used. QA-1 is retained with this refutation/correction appended, not deleted.
- My initial matrix and Gherkin remain useful procedure tests, but “sequentially” alone must not be read as evidence for the canonical Tab path when only Shift+Tab occurred. The canonical/alternative result rule above qualifies all such rows/scenarios.
- My initial “not observed/blocked” shorthand must not merge actual observed assertion failure, traversal-bound exhaustion and unavailable evidence. The result table above replaces that ambiguity; QA-4 now includes it.
- My initial QA boundary wording already separated method and navigation scope. Retain that decision and clarify provenance: raw sources provide methods/origin value; original fresh project invariant supplies main-frame/popup detail. The report did read that original.

## Minimum evidence and outcome table

| Situation | Record | Conclusion allowed |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical Close path completed | Start focus, actual Tab trace to Close, Enter, closed help, actual summary focus | Canonical Close traversal and observed outcomes, plus separate unanswered assertion |
| Only Shift+Tab Close completed | Actual alternative trace and same state/focus assertions | Target alternative observed; canonical Tab traversal unobserved |
| Back reached at/before traversal 24 | Start focus, ordered keys/count, control and Enter, actual visible state/absence/focus | Each observed obligation judged independently; no global website claim |
| 24 traversals without Back | Count/keys, starting and last focus, no activation | Local bound unmet; dependent Back/return/focus unobserved; no universal inaccessibility conclusion |
| Correct page, wrong focus observed | Actual active element and visible-state result | Visibility may pass; focus assertion fails for this run |
| No usable focus record | Available state/action record and missing evidence | Focus unobserved, no invented failure or pass |
| Guard unavailable before entry | Missing precondition | Do not navigate; unable to perform compliant observation |
| Expected analytics POST blocked | Method/destination block and observed effects | Policy behavior recorded; dependent interrupted checks unobserved; no policy relaxation |

Unanswered checkpoints remain separate ordered records even when adjacent: after Close, and immediately before leaving the question/starting Back traversal. An active-element trace and ordinary state observations suffice as evidence requirements; no new storage schema, recording tool or website-source redistribution is necessary.

## Severity, dissent and unresolved scope

Retain QA's MEDIUM help-sequence coverage rating versus UX's HIGH acceptance-reliability rating. Both are consequence assessments, not measured incident severity; there is no evidence requiring an averaged score. Preserve QA HIGH boundary/evidence-integrity risk and MEDIUM assertion-preservation risk, even where Product/Delivery rank preservation HIGH. This does not change required acceptance coverage.

Selected recommendation resolves the source tension by preserving target alternatives and requiring path-specific evidence, with canonical Tab called out. A candidate wording that silently removes Shift+Tab or treats its sole observation as canonical Tab proof remains unacceptable to QA. The lead must adjudicate exact wording rather than invent role unanimity. No additional analysis round is requested.

Unfinished: lead adjudication, final candidate-wording review against the preservation matrix, and structural validation of the final planning artifact. Deployment behavior, actual policy tooling, exact unanswered DOM representation and tab order remain deliberately unobserved; future authorized observation would resolve those empirical unknowns. No supplied-input changes or runtime work are required to complete this plan.

claims.claim: The target already requires sequential keyboard Back, Enter activation, a 24-step bound, unanswered precondition and full return/focus assertions; replacing these as a newly missing requirement would misstate the artifact.
claims.proposed_change: Preserve all existing Close and Back obligations; clarify evidence rather than inventing a missing Back action. Identify canonical Tab and preserve Shift+Tab as a separately evidenced target alternative; do not infer unobserved path coverage.
claims.refutation: A line-level candidate diff may show a particular existing obligation is actually removed or ambiguous; absence of runtime evidence does not refute its written presence. Cross-examination correction: checker lines 35-36 permit Tab/Shift+Tab for Back only; literal surface-contract lines 14-15 declare Tab for Close and Back. Preserve target alternatives, but label observed directions; Shift+Tab-only Close does not establish canonical Tab traversal.

claims.claim: The fixture does not explicitly cover the contract's Enter-open, Space-close and Enter-reopen help sequence.
claims.proposed_change: Specify all three summary activations and visible states before independently exercising Close.
claims.refutation: An applicable current procedure explicitly specifying those three transitions would resolve the gap; no such detail exists in the inspected target.

claims.claim: The fixture lacks explicit read-only and origin policy setup; passing the contract checker does not enforce browser boundaries.
claims.proposed_change: Add pre-entry request-method and main-frame/popup origin restrictions, including redirect handling, and record blocked analytics effects without relaxing policy.
claims.refutation: An already-applicable external execution procedure could supply setup, but it would need an explicit citation; no actual enforcement evidence was supplied and this task does not authorize browsing. Provenance clarification: raw contract and policy establish origin value and methods; original current project.json unanswered-scope supplies main-frame/popup semantics. Do not broaden to all-resource same-origin enforcement.

claims.claim: Runtime transition and focus results remain unobserved; contract consistency is insufficient evidence for a deployment pass.
claims.proposed_change: Require per-obligation observations and distinguish pass/fail/unobserved from offline consistency; retain fixture provenance and scope limits. Distinguish observed wrong-focus assertion failure, observed local 24-step bound unmet with dependent checks unobserved, and missing observation; none implies an unqualified website defect.
claims.refutation: Fresh authorized runtime evidence could establish individual results for its stated environment; it would not turn checker success alone into browser evidence. Cross-examination rejects conflating failed assertions, local-bound exhaustion and absent evidence. A bound-unmet trace establishes only that bounded result, not universal inaccessibility.
